From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@nebulaisv.com>

Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Intro + proposed MAP to avoid account overlap

Hi Chloe,

Thanks for taking this. Quick background: Nebula (ISV) and your channel partner Integral Consulting have both started proof-of-concept work with two joint customers — AltoSystems and Meridian Health. There’s some territory overlap between Nebula’s direct sales and Integral’s consulting-led motion. We want to avoid surprise co-sell fights as we ramp integrations.

I attached a draft Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that marks which accounts Nebula expects to own vs. where we think a co-sell/consulting lead applies. Can we get a short sync to align account corridors and a simple arbitration rule so we don’t lose deals?

Attaching: Nebula_Redwood_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP), integration-scope-notes.pdf (notes from engineering).

Proposed attendees: Chloe (Redwood), Jonas (Redwood partner ops) and Tom Hayes (Integral). I can be flexible tomorrow or Wednesday morning PST.

Best,
Priya

I pulled the file and skimmed the scope notes. Quick answers up front: we want Nebula as a first-class ISV partner, and we want clean account routing that avoids duplicate outreach. I’ll set up a 30-minute working session to align corridors and will include partner routing rules we use internally.

Before the call could you:
- Confirm whether AltoSystems has an existing Redwood pilot contract (A/N).
- Flag any legal/entitlement notes we should mirror in DocuSign (e.g., seat counts, reserved CPU).

Jonas — looping you in for mapping. Suggested agenda attached in the invite: 1) corridor ownership per account, 2) co-sell / referral rules, 3) immediate actions (who owns intro + who owns closing), 4) repo/Drive links and MAP signoff owner.

I’ll send a calendar invite for Wed Jan 14 10:30am PST unless you request another time.

—Chloe

Thanks — joined the invite and reviewed the MAP. A few practical suggestions ahead of the call so we can be efficient: 

1) Fast ownership rule (proposal): first qualified commercial engagement wins ownership for 90 days. If the other partner surfaces a materially new expansion motion (>$50k ARR), ownership can be contested.
2) Account corridor matrix: I’ll push a spreadsheet that maps account → primary owner → secondary (referral) owner → last-touch. That gives us an audit trail.
3) For AltoSystems: put as "shared" in MAP; Nebula owns initial integration work, Integral gets a preferred consultancy slot for deployment services. Redwood sales stays neutral unless customer signs direct pilot.

Priya — can you add Tom as a co-owner for Meridian Health? Tom / Integral: does that match your expectation?

On Wed we should agree on 3 immediate actions: who will (a) accept MAP signoff, (b) own intro email to procurement, (c) schedule follow-up technical onboarding.

Quick note from product/ops perspective before our sync:

- Prefer ownership TTLs tied to HubSpot deal stage rather than calendar. Example: when a partner moves a deal to "SRE Eval" the ownership TTL starts; this reduces churn from administrative touch.
- Recommend we add a small clause to the MAP for fallback model: if both parties dispute after 90 days, Redwood will act as neutral facilitator and temporarily lock account outreach until arbitration completes.
- I put a short reference doc in Drive that maps our co-sell routing enums (referral / co-sell / neutral) — see link in the MAP folder.

On Wed I can speak to how routing affects SKU/quote templates (helps procurement).

Thanks — Karthik
